2026 Paris Motor Show • Hyundai Tucson N Line Steals the Spotlight in Paris, but It's All Show and No Go
Toyota Tundra Goes Single Cab; It's a Short-Bed Sport Truck Now, Though Only Across Imagination Land
8 photos
Photo: abimelecdesign / Instagram
When Toyota Motor North America reported its September and third-quarter 2026 sales results, the highlights were on the electrified models and the namesake Toyota brand.
TMNA sold 201,306 vehicles, up 8.4 percent, in September 2026 across the US automotive market, and for the third quarter it reported deliveries of 633,223 vehicles, up 0.6 percent. The namesake Toyota division sold 171,469 vehicles during the past month, up 7.9 percent, while the quarter was finished with over 540k deliveries, up only 0.5%.
Year-to-date, TMNA reached 1,876,614 units, up 0.6%, while Toyota was up by 1.2% to almost 1.614 million vehicles, as Lexus dragged them down via its three-percent negative performance to less than 263k units. Anyway, Toyota can’t fully bank on the all-new RAV4 for its return to higher positive results because it’s still ramping up.
Instead, it got a helping hand from the Corolla, Camry, bZ, Corolla Cross, Grand Highlander, 4Runner, Sequoia, Sienna, and Tacoma nameplates. Not the bigger Tundra, though, which is slightly down by almost one percentage point. Well, the XK70 third generation is actually holding up pretty well given that it’s been around since the 2022 model year and so far, Toyota hasn’t issued a mid-cycle refresh procedure, only model year enhancements.
While we’re patiently waiting for the facelift, someone had an idea – a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, Abimelec Arellano, a virtual artist better known as " abimelecdesign " on social media, has prepared the newest wishful-thinking project - a cool Tundra truck.
His unofficial, hypothetical design project centers around the option of a Toyota Tundra Single Cab model with a short bed – aka a sport truck like in the good old days. To make it happen, he crafted a modified hood, lengthened the doors a little bit, along with the “bed in order to get those single cab proportions just right.” He also added “a ground effects kit and custom wheels,” and mixed a spectacular orange hue with black trim elements and a bedliner.
Last but not least, he asks us about the engine to be used with this potentially sporty model. Well, quite obviously, if the pixel master wanted our five cents on the matter, it would absolutely need the upcoming hybrid V8 used by the Gazoo Racing GR GT supercar. That way it could fight the 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT without breaking a sweat.
If that’s not possible even across Imagination Land, we’d think it suffices with the current 3.4 L V35A-FTS twin-turbo V6 rocking 437 hp. That way it might still compete with the entry-level tiers of the Rumble Bee and also with the Ford F-150 Lobo. What do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abimelec Arellano (@abimelecdesign)
